page: Google Cloud Platform m4n-ultramem-112 is an x86_64 architecture server configuration equipped with 112 dedicated vCPUs and 2976.0 GB of memory. Positioned in the Network Optimized family, this instance delivers an ultra-high memory ratio of approximately 26.57 GB per core. The instance includes no local storage volumes and provides zero GPU accelerators, requiring persistence and root filesystems to be provisioned via external network storage.

The hardware architecture focuses on memory density, consolidating nearly 3 TB of RAM within a single system image. Because dedicated CPU allocation is utilized, CPU contention is eliminated, though the complete lack of bundled local NVMe storage shifts all IOPS and throughput dependencies to network-attached block devices. Resource investment is concentrated heavily in volatile memory rather than local disk speed or hardware accelerators.

Given the 26.57 GB per vCPU memory-to-compute ratio, m4n-ultramem-112 is architected for applications requiring massive resident memory pools. Appropriate workloads include enterprise in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, large-scale Redis or Memcached clusters, in-memory graph processing, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise resource planning systems.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4n-ultramem-112 is an x86_64 server configuration belonging to the Network Optimized family, configured with 112 dedicated vCPUs and 2976.0 GB of system memory. Providing approximately 26.57 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance targets workloads with massive working set requirements. The configuration features zero GPUs and includes no local physical storage, relying entirely on external network-attached volumes for data retention and operating system files. The platform utilizes dedicated compute allocations, preventing vCPU oversubscription while centralizing large memory capacity into a single virtual machine environment. This resource distribution reduces overhead associated with multi-node clustering for memory-heavy applications. The m4n-ultramem-112 instance is designed for large in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise resource planning deployments, real-time telemetry processing, and in-memory analytics workloads.
